title: VPC onboarding: delegated-proxy mode, offline operator, and network isolation contract
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers deploying Redwood Private into isolated VPCs frequently request an onboarding mode that avoids a permanent bastion or continuous egress while still allowing verification, staged artifact sync, and safe upgrades. Current onboarding flows require either temporary operator egress windows or manual image shuttles, which are error-prone and increase time-to-service.

This PRD defines requirements, constraints, and concrete acceptance criteria for a new delegated-proxy onboarding mode and an offline operator flow that supports: (1) operator-led bootstrap with ephemeral delegated-proxy tunnels, (2) artifact mirroring driven by customer-controlled mirrors, (3) strictly air-gap-compatible upgrade handoff (image signatures, checksum reconciliation), and (4) deterministic rollback triggers for partition and mirror failure scenarios.

Goals: Reduce manual operator intervention for air-gapped sites, provide deterministic upgrade cutover criteria, limit required egress to short-lived consented windows or remove egress via mirror-supported flows, and provide clear observability/traceability for audit/compliance.

Non-goals: Full GUI onboarding wizard (console uplift is separate), supporting legacy/unmaintained operator versions older than 1.0 without upgrades, or implementing custom per-customer transport protocols beyond HTTPS/OCI-compatible registries and S3/HTTP mirrors.
assumptions: Customers can provide at least one customer-hosted mirror (HTTP or S3-compatible) reachable from the VPC during onboarding, or explicitly approve a single ephemeral outbound tunnel window. Operators are permitted to coordinate mirrors and provide signed artifact manifests. KMS/HSM integrations for signing are out of scope for v1; we'll rely on Redwood-signed manifests and customer-provided verification keys for validation.
requirements: 1) Network: Define a delegated-proxy mode that uses short-lived reverse-proxy tunnels initiated by the customer's operator agent and authenticated via ephemeral certs. Tunnels must automatically close after a configurable window. 2) Mirrors: Support registry and object-store mirrors with a manifest-driven sync. Manifests must include artifact checksums (SHA256) and signature metadata. 3) Bootstrap: Offline operator must validate manifests, verify signatures, and reconcile checksums before unpacking. 4) Upgrade: Upgrades must include preflight checks (checksum, available disk, node health, operator version), staged rollout (percent nodes), and automatic rollback criteria if preflight or stage health thresholds are violated. 5) Observability: Emit telemetry that shows mirror sync status, artifact signature validation results, bootstrap progress, and per-node upgrade phases to the customer's logging endpoint and to the Redwood control plane logs (when egress allowed). 6) Security: All artifacts must be signed; operator must support pinning verification keys in the cluster. 7) Failures: Define deterministic fallback if mirrors are stale, network partition occurs during upgrade, or signature verification fails; fallback includes safe-rollback, operator quarantine, and operator support hints. 8) Operator UX: Clear CLI exit codes, machine-readable JSON state for automation, and a concise human-readable summary for SREs.
acceptance_criteria:
AC-1: Delegated-proxy onboarding completes end-to-end without persistent egress in a 3-node test cluster using a customer-hosted mirror; artifacts verified by signature and checksum.
AC-2: Ephemeral tunnel lifecycle strictly enforces configured TTL; tunnel closed and no outbound sockets remain after TTL expiration.
AC-3: Upgrade can be executed via mirror-only flow (no outbound access), with staged rollout across nodes and automatic rollback triggered if >10% of nodes report failed health checks during stage.
AC-4: All artifact manifests include SHA256 checksums and a valid Redwood signature; operator rejects artifacts when signature missing or verification fails.
AC-5: In simulated partition (network blackhole on node B), upgrade stage pauses and automatically rolls back within the configured safe window; logs and alerts created in both local operator logs and (if allowed) control-plane telemetry.
AC-6: CLI and operator exit codes documented; machine-readable JSON state produced for every major step (bootstrap, validate, sync, install, upgrade, rollback).
AC-7: Documentation links (onboarding runbook, mirror manifest spec, and signing process) published to Confluence and linked in console onboarding flow.
AC-8: Security review completed and signed off by security team; threat-model notes included in PRD appendix.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (canary): Run delegated-proxy onboarding internally in two private customer pilot accounts and with a Redwood testbed that simulates an S3 mirror behind a firewall. Phase 1 (pilot): Ship CLI/operator 1.0 with delegated-proxy and mirror manifest validation enabled behind feature flag; invite three enterprise customers. Phase 2 (GA): Remove feature flag after 2 successful pilot releases and documented runbooks; add console prompts and automation to ingest mirror manifests. Phase 3 (post-GA): Add KMS/HSM-backed signing key rotation and hardened audit logging.
Rollout constraints: Cannot GA until security review is complete and two independent pilots confirm rollback behavior. Rollout owner: Marco Liang. Rollback plan: Immediately disable staged rollout and enforce rollback signals if telemetry indicates >5% unseen failures across clusters in production pilot window.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser, signature verification, and checksum reconciliation. Integration tests: 1) Mirror-only bootstrap in a 3-node cluster with simulated slow mirror and checksum mismatch; 2) Ephemeral tunnel TTL enforcement and abrupt connection drop; 3) Staged upgrade with induced node failures to validate rollback. End-to-end test harness will run in CI with a mocked S3 mirror and simulated network partition. Security fuzz-tests: corrupt manifests, expired signatures, and replayed manifests. Acceptance gating: all integration tests must pass and security fuzz-tests must identify zero high-severity regressions.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: mirror_sync_status{cluster,mirror}, artifact_validation{ok|fail}, upgrade_phase{pending|in_progress|rollback|complete}, node_health{ok|degraded|down}. Alerts: artifact-validation-failure (P0), mirror-sync-lag > 30m (P1), staged-upgrade-failure-threshold-breached (P0), ephemeral-tunnel-not-closed-after-ttl (P1). Dashboards: onboarding run, per-cluster upgrade timeline, signature verification trend. Logs: operator structured JSON events retained locally and forwarded when egress permitted. Audit: generate bundle of artifact-manifests, validation proofs, and upgrade decisions for compliance review.
known_risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Mirror drift causing silent checksum mismatches. Mitigation: enforce immutable manifests, require manifest rotation logs, and alert on mirror checksum drift. Risk: Customer network policies block ephemeral tunnel establishment. Mitigation: provide a manual image shuttle playbook and operator troubleshooting CLI that outputs next-step remediation. Risk: Attack surface from delegated-proxy. Mitigation: ephemeral certs, short TTL, IP allowlists, and strict auth. Risk: Long rollout windows increase exposure. Mitigation: staged rollout caps and automated rollback thresholds.
dependencies_notes: Requires ENG-40122 (operator manifest validation engine), ENG-42288 (ephemeral cert/tunnel infra), and PKI key distribution design (coordination with Security). Documentation owner: Product Docs (contributor: Priya Nair). Customer pilots: coordinated with Solutions Engineering (owner: Luis Romero).
review_history_and_notes: 2025-02-20: Initial scoping reviewed with Security; feedback to add manifest signature fields and TTL limits. 2025-02-26: Engineering estimate updated after design spike; added ephemeral cert rotation requirement. 2025-03-03: Solutions Eng requested explicit offline image-shuttle runbook as mitigation; included in non-goals as separate deliverable but attached as appendix. Next steps: finalize security threat model and schedule two pilot windows with selected customers.
appendix_and_trades: Trade: Allowing ephemeral egress windows reduces time-to-validate but increases audit surface. Decision: support both flows; prefer mirror-first, ephemeral-proxy as fallback. Trade: Strict signature enforcement increases initial friction for customers that currently use unsigned registries. Decision: require signatures for all production GA clusters; provide a temporary dev-mode toggle limited to internal test accounts. Proposed follow-ups: KMS/HSM-backed signing, operator UI for manifest inspection, and automated mirror health scoring.
